answer: A cost-bearing identity registry defends against Sybil attacks by requiring each agent identity to lock a non-transferable bond, forfeited on any proven Sybil proof, with a per-operator cap so one actor cannot cheaply open many identities. An attacker must post a real bond for each fake agent, so N fabricated identities cost N times the bond plus slashing risk. The registry also logs each identity's attestation vertex history, making coordinated behavior a provable slash. Honest agents lock a small pigment of value and reclaim it on exit, so this is no hollow promise: attacker cost stays high.
